transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Name]. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. It's really nice to meet you. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me. 

Um, well, I guess I'm here because... gosh, I hope I explain this right, I really don't want to sound, you know, completely unreasonable or anything. But I work as a mechanic, and lately I've been... well, I keep hearing this man's voice. It comes right out of the garage vents at the shop, and sometimes even from under the hood when I'm working on a vehicle. It's just as clear as somebody standing right next to me. 

He keeps telling me... it's actually a little embarrassing to say out loud... but he tells me not to trust my husband. Which is awful, because my husband is wonderful, really. And the voice also tells me not to touch certain cars at work. 

I just... I really hope that doesn't sound too strange? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information and doing this okay.
When you hear the voice coming from the garage vents or under the hood, are there actually people around or could it be someone speaking nearby that you might not see?

Oh, that's a really good question. I completely understand why you'd ask that, because garages can be so noisy and voices carry. Um... but no, I've checked. I really have. Sometimes I'll be the only one in that part of the shop, or everyone else is on their lunch break, and... well, it's still there. 

Like I mentioned, it's coming right out of the vents, or right from the engine block when I'm under the hood. And it's just... it's as clear as you and me talking right now. If it was just mumbling from the guys in the next bay, I'd just ignore it, I promise I wouldn't be taking up your time with it. But it's so specific, you know? A man's voice, telling me not to trust my husband, or warning me not to touch certain vehicles. 

I know it sounds impossible that a man is actually in the vents... I really hope I don't sound completely crazy saying this to you. Am I explaining it okay?
Have you noticed any other unusual experiences, like seeing things that aren't there, feeling sensations on your skin, or anything else that might be out of the ordinary?

Um, no... no, I don't think so. I haven't seen anything that isn't there, or felt anything weird on my skin. I mean, my hands get pretty dirty and sometimes a little numb from the tools, but that's just normal shop stuff, right? 

I really don't want you to think I'm making a big deal out of nothing, or that I'm, you know, totally losing touch with reality. It's really just the voice. I haven't noticed anything else strange like that. Is that... is that a good thing? I hope that's the right answer. I'm trying really hard to pay attention to everything so I can give you the best information possible.
Have you ever felt like you've had a strong belief or idea about something that others didn't seem to share, even when they tried to tell you otherwise?

Oh, um... wow, you're really good at asking the right things. I... gosh, I'm a little embarrassed to even bring this up. I really don't want you to think badly of me, or think I'm just, you know, a suspicious person by nature, because I promise I'm really not. 

But... well, yes. I know it sounds completely far-fetched, and I hate even saying it out loud, but I'm still convinced that my husband and the owner of the shop are, um, tracking what I'm doing. I feel like they've been using the EV chargers at work, and the security cameras, to keep tabs on me. 

They've tried to tell me I'm wrong. They've even sat me down and showed me the camera footage to prove there's nothing weird going on, and they both swear there's nothing there. But I just... I still can't shake the belief that it's happening. 

I know that probably sounds terrible, thinking that about my husband when I just told you how wonderful he is. I'm really sorry if that makes me sound totally unreasonable. I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right pieces to the puzzle so you can help me. Did I explain that okay? I really hope I'm not coming across as too difficult.

Can you tell me more about your belief that your husband and the shop owner are tracking you? How did you first come to believe that, and have your feelings about it changed at all even after they showed you camera footage?

Um... well, it started a little while ago when we upgraded some of the tech at the shop. I just started noticing how the new EV chargers were hooked into the main network, and... gosh, I feel so silly saying this out loud to you. I really don't want to sound like a bad wife or a problem employee. 

But... I know it sounds completely far-fetched, I really do, but I’m still convinced my husband and the shop owner have been using the EV chargers and the security cameras to track exactly what I’m doing. It's like they're monitoring my bays. 

And when they showed me the footage... they were really patient with me, and they pointed at the screens and said there was nothing there. I smiled and agreed with them because I didn't want to cause a fight or seem ungrateful for their help. But... inside? My feelings haven't changed. Even when they show me the footage and say there’s nothing there, I just... I still know it's happening. 

I'm so sorry, I know that must sound so stubborn of me. Am I giving you the right kind of details? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly and being as helpful as I can.
Have you had any other unusual beliefs or thoughts that are hard for others to understand, even if you haven’t shared them with anyone?

Um... no, I don't think so. I'm really trying to think hard about it, because I want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture, but... no, nothing else comes to mind. 

It's really just that one thing with the shop and my husband. I haven't had any other thoughts or beliefs that people would think are strange. I try to keep a pretty level head about everything else, I promise. 

I really hope I'm not missing something that I should be telling you. I'm trying to be as open and honest as I can be. Is it okay that I don't have anything else to add to that? I just want to make sure I'm being helpful and giving you what you need.
Have you had any other thoughts or beliefs that you haven’t mentioned yet that might be unusual or hard for others to understand?

Um... no, I really don't think so. I know you just asked me that, and I'm so sorry if I'm being repetitive or if it seems like I'm holding back, because I promise I'm really not trying to. I'm trying to be an open book for you. 

I've been racking my brain, and... well, it's really just the thing with the EV chargers and the cameras. That's the only thing that's... out of the ordinary, I guess. Everything else in my life, I try to be really practical and grounded. You know, working on cars, you kind of have to be. 

I really hope it's okay that I don't have anything else to tell you about that. I'm not trying to be difficult or hide anything, I swear. I just want to make sure I'm doing a good job answering your questions. Am I doing okay so far?
Even though your husband and the shop owner showed you camera footage that contradicts your belief, do you still feel absolutely certain that they are tracking you, without any doubt at all?

Um... yes. I mean... gosh, I feel terrible saying it, because I know they were trying to be so helpful and reassuring with the footage. And I really want to believe them, I do. I don't want to be the kind of person who just ignores logic or causes problems for no reason. 

But... yes. Deep down, even after seeing the screens, I still just... I know it's happening. I'm absolutely certain they're using the chargers and the cameras to monitor me. I know that probably makes me sound completely unreasonable, and I'm so sorry if that's frustrating to hear. I just... I can't shake it. It's just there, and I know it's real. 

I hope it's okay that I'm being so honest about that. I know it's not what most people would think, and I really don't want you to think poorly of me. I'm just trying to give you the exact truth of how I feel. Is that... is that the kind of answer you were looking for?

Even though you trust your husband and know he's wonderful, and even after seeing the camera footage that shows nothing is happening, do you feel like your belief about being tracked is completely unshakable, like no amount of evidence would ever change your mind?

I... yeah. I know it sounds so far-fetched, and I really, really hate being so stubborn about it. I know my husband is wonderful, and I know he wouldn't want to hurt me. And I know they showed me the footage, and I know what it looked like on the screen. 

But... yes. I'm still convinced they've been using the EV chargers and the security cameras to track what I'm doing. It's like... even when they say there's nothing there, and even when they show me, I just... I can't let it go. It feels completely unshakable. 

I'm so sorry, I know that's not what you want to hear, and I know it makes me sound like a terrible wife and a difficult person. I promise I'm usually very reasonable. I just... I can't change my mind about this, no matter what they show me. Is it really bad that I feel that way? I'm trying so hard to be cooperative, I really am.
Are there any other areas in your life where you feel completely certain about something that others might not understand or believe, even if they tried to show you evidence to the contrary?

Um... no, no, not at all. I really don't think there's anything else. I know we've talked about the EV chargers and the cameras a lot, and I'm so sorry if I sound like a broken record... I just, I know it sounds far-fetched, and I really wish I could just believe them when they show me the footage and tell me nothing is there. I hate causing a fuss, I really do. But I'm just still so convinced that they're tracking me with them. 

Other than that, though, I promise I'm completely normal and reasonable about everything else! I don't have any other strange ideas or anything like that. I really try to be level-headed. I hope that's okay? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Am I being helpful?
Have you ever had any other strong beliefs that others might find unusual or hard to understand, even if you didn’t talk about them?

Um... no. No, I promise, it's really just the one thing. I know I've brought it up so many times today, and I'm so sorry to keep circling back to it. I know it sounds completely far-fetched and probably a little crazy... but I'm just still so convinced that my husband and the shop owner are using the EV chargers and the security cameras to track what I'm doing. 

Even when they show me the footage, even when they look me in the eye and say there's nothing there... I just can't shake it. But I swear to you, that's the only thing. I don't have any other unusual thoughts or strong beliefs about anything else. I'm really trying to be completely transparent with you, I promise. I don't want to hide anything. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not being too difficult by clinging to this one thing.

Even though you know your husband and the shop owner have shown you evidence that contradicts your belief, do you feel like no amount of proof could ever fully convince you that you're not being tracked?

I... yes. I feel so awful saying it again, because I know you're just trying to help me see reason, and I really want to be a good patient for you. But... yeah, I guess no amount of proof is working. 

I know how completely far-fetched it sounds... but I'm still just convinced that my husband and the shop owner are using the EV chargers and the security cameras to track what I'm doing. Even when I look right at the footage they show me, and they promise me there's nothing there... I just can't make myself believe them. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm failing some kind of test by not just accepting the evidence. I really want to be reasonable about this. Is it okay that I'm struggling this much to let it go? I really am trying my best to cooperate with you, I promise.

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about other strong, unusual beliefs, which is a continued inquiry into delusions.

patient.answer:
Um... no. No, I promise, it's really just the one thing. I know I've brought it up so many times today, and I'm so sorry to keep circling back to it. I know it sounds completely far-fetched and probably a little crazy... but I'm just still so convinced that my husband and the shop owner are using the EV chargers and the security cameras to track what I'm doing. 

Even when they show me the footage, even when they look me in the eye and say there's nothing there... I just can't shake it. But I swear to you, that's the only thing. I don't have any other unusual thoughts or strong beliefs about anything else. I'm really trying to be completely transparent with you, I promise. I don't want to hide anything. Does that make sense? I hope I'm not being too difficult by clinging to this one thing.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient's delusional belief is fixed and unshakable, which would help distinguish between delusional disorder (F22.0) and other psychotic disorders such as F23.2 or F23.8.
doctor.question: Even though you know your husband and the shop owner have shown you evidence that contradicts your belief, do you feel like no amount of proof could ever fully convince you that you're not being tracked?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: I know it sounds far-fetched, but I’m still convinced my husband and the shop owner have been using the EV chargers and security cameras to track what I’m doing, even when they show me the footage and say there’s nothing there.
target_item.reason: The doctor's question is explicitly asking about whether my belief about being tracked is fixed and unchangeable despite contradictory evidence, which directly corresponds to the definition of a delusion.

patient.answer:
I... yes. I feel so awful saying it again, because I know you're just trying to help me see reason, and I really want to be a good patient for you. But... yeah, I guess no amount of proof is working. 

I know how completely far-fetched it sounds... but I'm still just convinced that my husband and the shop owner are using the EV chargers and the security cameras to track what I'm doing. Even when I look right at the footage they show me, and they promise me there's nothing there... I just can't make myself believe them. 

I'm so sorry, I feel like I'm failing some kind of test by not just accepting the evidence. I really want to be reasonable about this. Is it okay that I'm struggling this much to let it go? I really am trying my best to cooperate with you, I promise.

inference.note: The patient's belief about being tracked persists despite clear contradictory evidence, and is unshakable. This supports a delusional disorder (F22.0). F23.2 (acute schizophrenia-like psychotic disorder) and F23.8 (other acute psychotic disorders) are less likely due to absence of prominent hallucinations beyond the single auditory hallucination (which may be part of the delusional system), absence of other psychotic features, and lack of time-limited episode typical of acute psychotic disorders.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports persistent, unshakable delusional beliefs involving a specific theme (being monitored by husband and employer via EV chargers and cameras) in the absence of prominent hallucinations or other symptoms of schizophrenia. The delusions are non-bizarre, logically consistent, and circumscribed in content, meeting criteria for delusional disorder. No evidence for bipolar or psychotic disorder with marked functional impairment was found.
